commits: Add test. | Add a changelog. | Fix FiniteElement::has_support_points() for FE_Nothing.
cl: Fixed: The FiniteElement::has_support_points() function is poorly named because it does not return *whether* an element has support points, but whether it *implements* the FiniteElement::get_unit_support_points() function correctly. Because of this misunderstanding, it returned `false` for the FE_Nothing element. This is now fixed: FE_Nothing::has_support_points() now returns `true`, because the empty array returned by FE_Nothing::get_unit_support_points() correctly describes the support points the element has (namely: it does not have any, as there are no degrees of freedom). (Wolfgang Bangerth, 2024/05/19)

commits: Add a changelog entry about fixing a bug. | Add a changelog. | Make the curl in 2d a true scalar. | Avoid using 'scalar_product' in favor of 'operator*'.
cl: Changed: In three space dimensions, the curl of a vector field is unambiguously a three-dimensional vector. In two space dimensions, it is typically defined as a scalar, interpreted as the magnitude of a vector aligned with the $z$-axis the results from taking the curl of a vector field that lives in the $x-y$ plane. For historical reasons, deal.II used to represent this scalar as a Tensor<1,1> (i.e., a tensor of rank one -- a tensor with one index -- for which the only possible value of the index is zero). This is, of course, entirely equivalent to it being a scalar, but it is semantically wrong: The data type should have been a scalar, not an array of which one can take the zeroth element.

title: Fix broken explicit instantiations in trilinos_tpetra_precondition_frosch.cc
commits: Fix broken explicit instantiations in trilinos_tpetra_precondition_frosch.cc
cl: Fixed: The explicit instantiations of LinearAlgebra::TpetraWrappers::PreconditionFROSch::initialize() for the float scalar type declared a non-const DoFHandler argument and therefore did not match the declaration, and one instantiation in the complex-double block was malformed. As a consequence deal.II failed to compile against a Trilinos configured with Tpetra_INST_FLOAT=ON and ShyLU_DDFROSch. (Ernesto Ismail, 2026/08/25)

title: Add missing Number() cast in the ReadWriteVector min branch
commits: Add missing Number() cast in the ReadWriteVector min branch
cl: Fixed: When importing a Tpetra vector with VectorOperation::min, ReadWriteVector assigned the value from the Kokkos view without converting it to the vector's number type, unlike the surrounding insert, add and max branches. This made deal.II fail to compile whenever the Kokkos scalar type differed from the ReadWriteVector number type. (Ernesto Ismail, 2026/08/25)

title: Use the matrix and vector scalar type in MatrixScaling
commits: Use the matrix and vector scalar type in MatrixScaling
cl: Fixed: MatrixScaling assumed that the scalar type of a distributed matrix or vector is double. As a consequence deal.II failed to compile against a PETSc configured with complex scalars, because PetscScalar is then std::complex<double>. The arrays passed to the matrix and vector set() functions now use the scalar type of the matrix and vector respectively. (Ernesto Ismail, 2026/08/25)

title: Guard TpetraWrappers::Vector::min() with if constexpr
commits: Guard TpetraWrappers::Vector::min() with if constexpr
cl: Fixed: LinearAlgebra::TpetraWrappers::Vector::min() guarded complex number types with a run-time assertion, but its body still had to compile for every instantiated type and used operator< as well as std::numeric_limits::max(), neither of which is defined for complex numbers. The body is now guarded with if constexpr, so that deal.II can be compiled against a Trilinos providing complex Tpetra instantiations. (Ernesto Ismail, 2026/08/26)

title: Skip artificial cell when sorting particles
commits: Add a unit test | Indent | Skip artificial cell when sorting particles
cl: Fixed: Particles::ParticleHandler::sort_particles_into_subdomains_and_cells() also searched artificial cells when looking for the new cell of a particle. A particle found in such a cell was then scheduled to be sent to numbers::artificial_subdomain_id, which triggered an assertion in debug mode and silently deleted the particle in release mode without emitting the particle_lost signal. Artificial cells are now skipped, so that these particles are correctly reported as lost. This behavior is checked by the new test particles/particle_handler_sort_03. (Bruno Blais, 2026/08/31)

title: Improve initial guess and robustness in `MappingFE::transform_real_to_unit_cell()`
commits: MappingFE::transform_real_to_unit_cell: improve robustness
cl: Fixed: MappingFE::transform_real_to_unit_cell() now starts the Newton iteration from the inverse of the affine map through the vertices for simplices and from the barycenter of the reference cell otherwise, instead of the origin of the reference cell, and halves the Newton step until the residual decreases. If the iteration does not converge from the affine map or converges to a point outside of the reference cell, it is restarted from the barycenter. For a point outside of the cell, the result closest to the reference cell is returned. This improves robustness for curved cells of all types. title: AlignedVector::insert(): fix the computational complexity.
commits: AlignedVector::insert(): fix the computational complexity.
cl: Changed: Like for std::vector, the range passed to AlignedVector::insert() may no longer refer to elements of the vector itself. In debug mode, this is checked for ranges of the vector's value type by testing the addresses of the first and the last element of the range. Copy such a range into a separate container before inserting it. (David Wells, 2026/11/11) Fixed: AlignedVector::insert() now reuses the existing capacity and grows the allocation geometrically when it needs more memory. Previously, every call reallocated the whole array to exactly the new size, so inserting elements one at a time had quadratic complexity. (David Wells, 2026/11/10)

title: GMRES: Add Kokkos kernels for orthogonalization with device vectors
commits: Fix for older Kokkos version | Changelog | GMRES: Add Kokkos kernels for orthogonalization with device vectors
cl: Improved: SolverGMRES and SolverFGMRES now use optimized Kokkos kernels for the classical Gram-Schmidt and the delayed classical Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization with LinearAlgebra::distributed::Vector in MemorySpace::Default. The inner products against all basis vectors are computed in a single sweep with a single synchronization and MPI reduction per step, and the vector updates are fused into one sweep. (Martin Kronbichler, 2026/11/17)

title: FEEvaluation: fix RT gradient after submit_value
commits: FEEvaluation: fix RT gradient after submit_value
cl: Fixed: FEEvaluation::get_gradient() for FE_RaviartThomasNodal on cells that are not parallelograms used the values on the unit cell, which FEEvaluation::submit_value() overwrites. Calling submit_value() before get_gradient() for the same quadrature point, as in a loop that submits both values and gradients, gave wrong gradients. FEEvaluation and FEFaceEvaluation now keep a copy of these values for get_gradient(). (Richard Schussnig, 2026/11/20)
